name: Carry On Rhy

originals.guitar: Unconfirmed (Kiko Loureiro is associated with Ibanez superstrats; model on the 1993 recording not found)

guitar.position: bridge pickup for rhythm, tone knob around 8-10; neck pickup with tone rolled slightly back for the lead
guitar.tone_notes: Could not confirm the guitars from sources; the pickup type is an assumption from the high-gain power-metal sound. A single-coil guitar will sound thinner: add a little gain and roll back treble.

band.style_feel: fast driving double-time metal, straight eighths, snare on 2 and 4 (or half-time feel at 80)
parts: Part A: intro riff - two-guitar riff, drums tight
Part B: verse - sparser, minor progression
Part D: chorus - full band, open and big
Part E: solo - same drive as the verse
band.tips: Tempo and key are Spotify-derived estimates (songbpm.com) and the song is recorded half a step down, so check against the record. Play the intro riff cleanly for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning; keep palm-muted 8ths steady.

whammy.tuning: Eb standard (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb), unverified
whammy.when: Whole song, only if you want to match the record's pitch
how: Tune your guitar to standard (E A D G B E).
Turn the right knob to TRANSPOSE DOWN 1.
Press DROPTUNE (light on) before the song.
whammy.tips: Could not verify the tuning from an authoritative source: user-submitted tabs on Ultimate Guitar list Eb standard for Carry On, but one file lists E standard, and no source confirms which is the guitar tuning on the record. No whammy sweep or octave part was found. Skip the pedal if you prefer to play in standard tuning, or check by ear against the record.

memo: Angra - Carry On: rhythm. Tight, scooped-mid high-gain power-metal chug (Ibanez + Marshall/Mesa-style stack, 90s Helloween-school sound), Brown amp with a boost for tightening.

name: Carry On Lead
memo: Angra - Carry On: lead. Singing neo-classical lead, more gain and mids for sustain, delay and plate reverb.
